rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Jiaoren, the pearl-weeping South Sea weaver.
ANATOMY: One merperson-like humanoid head with normal small rounded HUMAN ears, two eyes, two arms. NO fin ears, NO webbing, NO horns, NO gills or fish facial parts. Wear PLAIN OPAQUE HIGH-NECK LONG-SLEEVE CLOTH that covers chest, shoulders, arms and entire torso completely. Lower aquatic anatomy is hidden beneath water and full folds of cloth because source does not detail it [merperson-in-southsea-c01, merperson-in-southsea-c05]. No jewellery.
MOMENT: Looks DIRECTLY toward viewer in a fierce sorrowful confrontation while two streams of tears from both eyes turn visibly into round white pearls. Both hands pull a broad length of woven cloth taut in front of the churning water, physically engaged at peak of the motion.
POWER: Tears become pearls as they leave the eyes, pearls falling onto cloth; the special woven cloth stays visibly dry surrounded by ocean water [merperson-in-southsea-c03, merperson-in-southsea-c04, merperson-in-southsea-c05]. NO other powers.
SCALE & CAMERA: Low close frontal half-body view, eyes and pearl streams large enough to read at 200px. No giant size.
LIGHT & WEATHER: Low-key deep walnut water, one narrow antique-gold dusk side light, deep painterly shadows, salty surface droplets with no magical light.
SURFACE: Expressive traditional oil-brush texture, tactile dry woven cloth, heavy dark waves.
SETTING: South Sea [merperson-in-southsea-c01].
MOOD: Uncanny imposing mythological pearl-weeping presence and strong physical cloth action, not placid portrait.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: No text, lettering, pseudo-writing, marks, symbols, logo, border or watermark; no invented fins/ears/gills/scales on human head, no extra limbs/digits; no jewellery, no transparent fabric, bare shoulders, chest, nudity or gore; no aura, neon, rays, energy or copyrighted design.

Uji Sangar 1–7 YES: frontal uncanny pearl-weeping weaver dominates frame, physically pulls cloth, pearl tears c03/c05 and dry cloth c04 read at 200px; normal human upper face/2 arms covered in opaque cloth with hidden undescribed lower form, no fin ears/text/glow/IP. root_visual_review.notes: The pearl tears work on the native crop, but at normal and thumbnail size this reads as an ordinary young woman crying at the shoreline holding a cloth — the 'ordinary woman at human scale' failure. Nothing shows a being that lives in water like a fish [merperson-in-southsea-c05, c07]. Keep the pearl tears and the woven cloth, but set her fully underwater, weaving at a loom on the South Sea floor, the jiao cloth staying dry and unrippled while her hair, the water and fish move around it [c04, c06, c07]; pearls drop from her eyes and sink. Still no invented fish tail, fin ears or jewellery.
